prompt: Annex A marks which two items under Own Situation as ASSUMED?
options: Organizational structure of forces; disposition and location
Capabilities of friendly forces; inventory of signal assets and reserves
Status of personnel and training profile; inventory of signal assets
Status of personnel and training profile; capabilities
explanation: Annex A (PAM 6-0102 PDF page 44): under Own Situation, items c and d, the status of personnel and training profile and the inventory of signal assets, are marked ASSUMED.

prompt: Which statement about revising a signal estimate is correct?
options: It is revised only at mission analysis
It is revised as the situation changes and new facts are introduced
It is fixed once the commander approves it
It is revised only when the enemy course of action changes during the operation
explanation: PAM 6-0102 para 0302: the signal estimate is revised as the situation changes and new facts are introduced.

prompt: After separate estimates are made for each signal support service and C4S capability, what does the signal officer do?
options: Publishes each as a separate annex
Selects the one with the most capability
Integrates them
Hands them to the S3 unchanged
explanation: PAM 6-0102 para 0302 allows separate estimates; the handout (p. 3) adds that the signal officer then integrates them.

prompt: Why does the signal estimate examine its factors?
options: To list every available radio, its serviceability, and the operator assigned to it during the operation
To forecast the enemy's next movement
To decide which staff section leads the operation
To determine their effect on the successful accomplishment of the signal support operations mission
explanation: PAM 6-0102 para 0302: the estimate examines factors, known or assumed, that may affect successful accomplishment of the signal support operations mission.

prompt: In the Annex A format, terrain, weather and existing communications are analyzed with which METAL factor?
options: Enemy signal capabilities
Area of Operations
Troops
Mission
explanation: PAM 6-0102 para 0303 names the Area of Operations as the A in METAL, and Annex A places terrain, weather and existing communications in the AO and AI analysis.

prompt: A shortage of qualified operators may limit a COA. Under which METAL factor and Annex A entry is this finding recorded?
options: Logistical requirements; inventory of signal assets
Mission; capabilities
Area of operations; existing communications
Troops; status of personnel and training profile
explanation: PAM 6-0102 para 0303 names the Troops available to accomplish the mission, and Annex A records personnel status under Own Situation.

prompt: A COA needs an extra resupply trip to remain usable. Which METAL factor and Annex A item capture this?
options: Troops; personnel requirements and the roster of operators
Area of operations; existing communications
Logistical requirements; sustainment requirements
Enemy; capabilities and limitation
explanation: PAM 6-0102 para 0303 names the Logistical requirements needed to assure the mission's success, and Annex A Section V item C records sustainment requirements.

prompt: The staff learns that an opposing force can interfere with a type of communications system. Which METAL factor and Annex A section record it?
options: Troops; Own Situation
Area of operations; Situation and COA
Enemy; Analysis of Opposing COA
Mission; Mission paragraph
explanation: PAM 6-0102 para 0303 names the Enemy signal capabilities, and Annex A Section III analyzes the opposing COA and the enemy's capabilities and limitations.

prompt: Where does the baseline description of an already operating communications system belong in Annex A?
options: Capabilities, under Analysis of Opposing COA
Capabilities, under Own Situation
Means of communication, under Decision/Recommendations
Existing communications, under Situation and COA
explanation: Annex A (PAM 6-0102 PDF page 44): Section II, Situation and COA, has item C, Existing Communications, in the AO and AI analysis.

prompt: Item C of Section III, Analysis of Opposing COA, lists what?
options: Enemy capabilities and limitations, obtained through an RFI from Intel
Friendly forces capabilities and limitations, obtained through the S6 section
Counter-measures against the enemy capabilities
The communication and disposition of opposing forces
explanation: Annex A: Section III item C lists the enemy capabilities and countermeasures (RFI from Intel); items D and E cover friendly capabilities and counter-measures.

prompt: Which Section III item assesses the expected reach of the opposing forces' communications?
options: Signal propagation of opposing forces
Communication and disposition of opposing forces
List of enemy capabilities and countermeasures
Counter-measures
explanation: Annex A: Section III item B is the signal propagation of opposing forces.

prompt: Under Counter-measures in Annex A, which two sub-entries are shown?
options: Capabilities of the signal platoon; limitations of the enemy
On the enemy capabilities; signal platoon limitations
Enemy structure; enemy strength
Propagation; disposition
explanation: Annex A: Section III item E, Counter-measures, has two entries: on the enemy capabilities and signal platoon limitations.

prompt: A COA depends on an assumed asset inventory. How does Annex A treat those items?
options: They are marked as assumed under Own Situation
They are treated as verified facts once the COA is selected
They are deleted from the estimate
They are moved to the Decision section
explanation: Annex A (PAM 6-0102 PDF page 44): the status of personnel and the inventory of signal assets are marked ASSUMED, and the estimate is revised as facts replace them.

prompt: The Comparison of COAs section builds directly on which earlier section?
options: Decision/Recommendations
Mission
Analysis of Opposing COA
Situation and COA
explanation: Annex A: Section III, Analysis of Opposing COA, comes immediately before Section IV, Comparison of COAs.

prompt: Which METAL factor captures the difference in sustainment effort between two COAs?
options: Logistical requirements
Troops
Mission
Area of operations
explanation: PAM 6-0102 para 0303: the Logistical requirements factor covers what is needed to assure the mission's success, including sustainment.

prompt: A Comparison slide only repeats each option's description. What should it show instead?
options: Relative strengths and limitations against the mission
The history and development of each option under consideration
The enemy's preferred COA
The equipment list for each option
explanation: Annex A: Section IV, Comparison of COAs, weighs the friendly options against each other to support the decision.

prompt: A trained operator can be reallocated to cover a personnel shortage. Under which Section V item is the recommendation recorded?
options: C4S requirements
Sustainment requirements
Personnel requirements
Task list
explanation: Annex A: Section V item A, Personnel Requirements, carries the recommendation for personnel.

prompt: Where should an ongoing battery supply need for the recommended COA be entered?
options: C4S requirements
Sustainment requirements
Personnel requirements and skills
Means of communication
explanation: Annex A: Section V item C, Sustainment Requirements, carries the recommendation for supply needs such as generator sets and batteries.

prompt: Which Section V item records the proposed locations of the TCP and MCP?
options: Means of communication and PACE
Location of TCP and MCP
C4S requirements
Task list
explanation: Annex A: Section V item E is the location of the TCP and MCP.

prompt: Which Section V item states the communication method that supports the preferred COA?
options: C4S requirements
Task list
Means of communication
Location of TCP and MCP
explanation: Annex A: Section V item D, Means of Communication, states the method that supports the recommended COA.

prompt: What does the handout direct for an assumption that does not affect the solution?
options: Keep it as a fact
Verify it before the next step
Drop it
Move it to the task list
explanation: Handout p. 5: replace assumptions with facts as information comes in, and drop any assumption that does not affect the solution.

prompt: Which of the five steps assembles facts and assumptions, determines the signal means for each COA and screens them?
options: Step 1, know the problem and state the signal mission
Step 2, gather data and determine possible solutions
Step 3, analyze the solutions
Step 4, compare the solutions
explanation: Handout p. 5: Step 2 assembles facts and assumptions, determines the signal means or concepts that could support each unit COA, and screens them.

prompt: Can the enemy intercept, jam, direction-find or attack sites? This question belongs to which METT-TC variable and METAL factor?
options: Mission, and M for the mission
Enemy, and E for enemy signal capabilities
Troops and support available, and T for troops
Terrain and weather, and A for area of operations
explanation: Handout p. 4: the enemy variable asks about interception, jamming, direction-finding, site attack, cyber and drones, which is the E factor.

prompt: Which METT-TC variable asks which signal tasks are specified or implied and which nets must be entered or provided?
options: Enemy
Troops and support available
Time available
Mission
explanation: Handout p. 4: the signal questions for the Mission variable are which signal tasks are specified or implied and which nets must be entered or provided.

prompt: Under paragraph 1b, characteristics of the area of operations, which enemy details are listed?
options: Committed and uncommitted signal elements, equipment status, training and morale
EW units, congested parts of the spectrum, C4S capabilities, weaknesses
Existing commercial systems and the security of using them
Terrain and weather, propagation, line of sight, critical periods
explanation: Handout p. 6: paragraph 1b lists EW units, congested parts of the spectrum, C4S capabilities and weaknesses under the enemy; the other lists are friendly C4S resources, civil considerations and terrain.

prompt: What does the handout say about a COA that fails the tactical requirement?
options: It is rejected, since failing the tactical requirement is a disadvantage that rules it out
It is accepted if it saves the most signal personnel, even though it fails the tactical requirement
It is ranked last but kept for comparison
It is accepted with a recommendation to mitigate
explanation: Handout p. 7: failure to meet the tactical requirement is usually a disadvantage, and such a COA is rejected.

prompt: When two COAs end with equal weighted totals, what does the handout tell the S6 to do?
options: Select the COA that was listed first
Add a new criterion and repeat the matrix until one total is lower than the other
Choose the COA that uses fewer signal personnel
Compare criterion by criterion and explain the trade-off to the commander
explanation: Handout p. 7: when totals tie, the S6 compares criterion by criterion and explains the trade-off; the matrix supports the recommendation but does not make it.

prompt: A recommendation states the most supportable COA and what else?
options: The total of each weighted ranking, shown for every COA and every criterion
The enemy's likely reaction to each COA
The list of unserviceable equipment
What the signal elements will do: who, what, when, where, how and why
explanation: Handout p. 7: state which COA is most supportable and what the signal elements will do to support it: who, what, when, where, how and why.

prompt: In the Mindoro example, VHF tactical radios have dead spots behind the mountain ranges. What does the terrain analysis propose?
options: Relay or repeater stations on key terrain, with HF radios under the mountains
More VHF handheld radios issued to every squad moving through the mountain ranges
Messengers on all mountain approaches
Cellular phones as the only means in the mountains
explanation: Lesson slides 23 and 24: Mount Iglit and Mount Halcon are key terrain for relay or repeater stations, and HF radios matter most under the mountains.

prompt: Which effects does the lesson's weather analysis record?
options: Thunderstorms limit HF radios, and daytime heat affects the ionosphere for VHF
Thunderstorms limit UHF radios, and high humidity limits HF
Heavy winter rain limits VHF radios, and cold nights limit HF
Thunderstorms limit VHF radios, and daytime heat affects the ionosphere for HF
explanation: Lesson slides 25 and 26: early evening thunderstorms and showers limit VHF tactical radios, and high daytime temperature affects the ionosphere and the HF modulating signal.

prompt: In the Para IV comparison, what disadvantage is recorded for COA 5, total radio listening silence?
options: No C2 will be established
Repeaters cannot be installed
Cellular sites are exposed
The enemy detects all transmissions
explanation: Lesson slide 49: COA 5 deceives enemy information gathering, but its disadvantage is that no C2 will be established.

prompt: Which entry belongs in the task list of Para V?
options: A generator set and ten Harris handheld radios, to be supplied by the sustainment section
A cybersecurity specialist as a required skill
PACE arrangements for each net
Install an SMVRS and a co-located UHF repeater, to be done by the signal platoon
explanation: Lesson slides 52 and 58: the task list is the commander's decision and includes installing the SMVRS and UHF repeater by the signal platoon; the other choices belong to the sustainment, personnel and means-of-communication items.
